newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler says EMU deficit goal becoming a benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler says EMU deficit goal becoming a benchmark.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz Christoph Zeitler said on Monday the Maastricht Treaty's three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) deficit criterion for entry into European monetary union was becoming a "benchmark" in financial markets.

Zeitler said in an opinion piece to be published on Tuesday in the Handelsblatt newspaper that the deficit criterion has taken on a life of its own as a standard against which to measure who will be able to join the euro at its start in January 1999.

"Public explanations from major Asian governments show that the three percent deficit criteria in the meantime is playing a role in international financial markets," the newspaper quoted Zeitler as writing in a statement ahead of publication.
Zeitler said a clear interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria was important to guarantee a credible currency after its launch.
"What will happen in currency union must also apply to the solution of who enters," the statement quoted Zeitler as writing.
